title: MSE with iamse
text: Next define simulation settings check.set(). vignette use small number projection years replicates.
code: set <- check.set()  ## Number of projection years set$nysim <- 20  ## Number of stochastic replicates (kept small for demonstration) set$nrep <- 10  ## Use the median across replicates as reference method set$refMethod <- "median"

title: MSE with iamse
text: now specify variation life history, process, observation components. entry given three-element vector interpreted inside iamse.
code: ## Between-replicate variation (life-history parameters) set$noise$rep$H  <- c(0.1, 0, 1) set$noise$rep$M  <- c(0.1, 0, 1) set$noise$rep$R0 <- c(0.1, 0, 1)  ## Process noise (recruitment and fishing mortality) set$noise$time$R <- c(0.7, 0.4, 1)   ## species-specific recruitment variability set$noise$rep$F  <- c(0.15, 0, 1)  ## Observation noise (indices and catches) set$noise$time$I <- c(0.3, 0, 1) set$noise$time$C <- c(0.1, 0, 1)

title: Intra-Annual Management Strategy Evaluation (IAMSE)
text: Explicit intra-annual dynamics (e.g. seasons quarters) operating model. Length-based growth, selectivity, mortality can included data allow. Flexible, stochastic age–length conversion link length-based observations age-based dynamics. title: Intra-Annual Management Strategy Evaluation (IAMSE)
text: package installed loaded, typical workflow : Prepare life-history stock data check.dat(). Set simulation noise settings check.set(). Estimate reference points (deterministic stochastic). Define one HCRs (e.g. def.hcr.conscat(), def.hcr.ref(), def.hcr.spict()). Run MSE run.mse(). Summarise visualise results using plotiamse.*() est.metrics() functions. basic example (mirroring demo vignette):
code: library(iamse)  ## Example life-history data data("stocklist") dat0 <- stocklist$mlh dat0$CVlen <- 0.1 dat  <- check.dat(dat0)  ## Simulation settings set <- check.set() set$nysim   <- 20   # projection years set$nrep    <- 10   # number of replicates (low for demo) set$refMethod <- "median"  ## Noise structure (simplified) set$noise$rep$H  <- c(0.1, 0, 1) set$noise$rep$M  <- c(0.1, 0, 1) set$noise$rep$R0 <- c(0.1, 0, 1) set$noise$time$R <- c(0.7, 0.4, 1) set$noise$rep$F  <- c(0.15, 0, 1) set$noise$time$I <- c(0.3, 0, 1) set$noise$time$C <- c(0.1, 0, 1)  ## Stochastic reference points set$refN <- 100 dat <- est.ref.levels.stochastic(dat, set, fmax = 5,                                  ncores = 2, plot = TRUE)  dat$ref$Blim <- 0.2 * dat$ref$B0  ## Define some HCRs iamse::def.hcr.ref(set. = set)                      # "noF" iamse::def.hcr.ref(consF = "fmsy", set. = set)      # "refFmsy" iamse::def.hcr.conscat(set. = set)                  # "conscat"  set$hcr <- c("noF", "refFmsy", "conscat")  ## Run MSE (single core for portability) resMSE <- run.mse(dat, set, ncores = 1, verbose = TRUE)  ## Plot time series par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1)) plotiamse.f(dat, set, resMSE) plotiamse.cw(dat, set, resMSE) plotiamse.b(dat, set, resMSE)

Typical elements include quantiles predicted catch reference points, e.g. `list(catch = 0.5, ffmsy = 0.5, bbmsy = 0.5, bmsy = 0.5, fmsy = 0.5)`. Values probabilities \[0, 1]. breakpointB Numeric biomass breakpoint (scale \(B/B_{MSY}\) related indicator) can modify rule given biomass level (e.g. conservative advice biomass low). evalBreakpointB Numeric integer specifying breakpoint evaluated (e.g. period using biomass indicator). exact interpretation depends internal implementation. safeguard List describing additional biomass safeguard, typically form `list(limitB = <threshold>, prob = <probability>)`. example, rule may reduce cap TAC probability biomass `limitB` exceeds `1 - prob`. dteuler Time step forward Euler scheme used SPiCT solve underlying continuous-time model. Default `1/4` (quarterly). reportmode Integer flag passed SPiCT controlling level detail reporting output. stabilise Numeric logical argument passed SPiCT's `stabilise` option, controlling strongly SPiCT fit stabilised (e.g. presence limited data). Default `0` (additional stabilisation). priorlogn Numeric vector giving prior initial depletion (log scale), typically form `c(mean, sd, p)` `p` indicator controlling whether prior active. priorlogsdf Numeric vector giving prior process-noise standard deviation fishing mortality (log scale). priorlogsdc Numeric vector giving prior process-noise standard deviation catches (log scale). priorlogalpha Numeric vector giving prior production function exponent \(\alpha\) (log scale). priorlogbeta Numeric vector giving prior production function exponent \(\beta\) (log scale). priorlogbkfrac Numeric vector giving prior fraction carrying capacity biomass starts (log scale). priorlogr Numeric vector giving prior intrinsic growth rate \(r\) (log scale). fixn Optional value indicating whether depletion parameter (`n`) fixed SPiCT fit. Default `NA` means estimated. bfac Optional numeric factor used scale biomass-based reference points computing advice. Default `NA` means additional scaling. bref Character string specifying biomass reference level defined, e.g. `"current"`, `"lowest"`, `"highest"`, `"average"` `"last"`. reference used together `brefType`, `nyBref`, `btar` construct biomass-based triggers. brefType Character string specifying type biomass reference, typically `"target"` `"limit"`. affects conservative rule becomes biomass near reference. nyBref Integer giving number years used define biomass reference (e.g. average biomass last `nyBref` years). btar Character string specifying target biomass level used rule, e.g. `"bmsy"` biomass MSY. probtar Numeric probability (\[0, 1]) indicating conservative target rule (e.g. requiring probability `btar` exceeds `probtar`). brule Numeric code scaling factor controlling biomass rule applied target (e.g. linear reduction, aggressive reductions, reduction). red Optional numeric reduction factor applied advised catch additional criteria met (e.g. low biomass, repeated assessment failure). example, `0.8` corresponds 20% reduction. `NA`, reduction applied. redyears Integer indicating many years reduction criteria evaluated (e.g. number years threshold reduction triggered). redAlways Logical; `TRUE`, reduction rule evaluated applied every time criteria met. `FALSE`, reduction may applied sparingly, depending internal implementation. rai Numeric "raising factor" controls quickly rule responds moving back towards higher catches (e.g. reduction). Default `0.2`. manstartdY Numeric management start year offset relative assessment time series (e.g. `0` last year, negative values earlier years). Default `0`. assessmentInterval Positive integer giving interval (years) full SPiCT assessments advice updates. Default `1`, .e. annual assessments. cpvec Logical; `TRUE`, use vector catch profiles control points computing advice. Default `FALSE`. halfAssessInt Logical; `TRUE`, assessment effectively shifted half assessment interval (e.g. mid-year updates). Default `FALSE`. intC Numeric `NA`. non-`NA`, can used specify predefined catch level initial period interval. Default `NA`. nonconvHCR Character string giving name alternative HCR used SPiCT assessment converge. Default `"conscat"`, typically corresponds constant-catch rule defined [def.hcr.conscat()]. clType Character string specifying type control variable returned HCR, e.g. `"TAC"` catch advice. Used combination stabilisation cap. clyears Integer giving number years used compute reference level stabilisation cap (e.g. mean catch last `clyears` years). Default `1`. stab Logical; `TRUE`, apply uncertainty stabilisation cap limits year--year changes advice (e.g. TAC). Default `FALSE`. lower Numeric lower bound stabilisation cap, typically interpreted minimum allowed ratio \(\text{Advice}_{y+1} / \text{Advice}_y\). Default `0.8` (maximum 20% decrease). upper Numeric upper bound stabilisation cap, typically interpreted maximum allowed ratio \(\text{Advice}_{y+1} / \text{Advice}_y\). Default `1.2` (maximum 20% increase). bm Logical numeric. `FALSE` (default), explicit benchmarks applied. positive integer supplied (e.g. `5`), biomass reference `Bref` may redefined every `bm` years (benchmarking). env Environment generated HCR function(s) created stored.
